selection.diff_summary:
Summary: Adds a new LoopVectorize/VPlan test subdirectory and several VPlan printing tests for RISCV, PowerPC, and AArch64. The retrieved hunks are entirely test-only and assert specific VPlan recipe ordering and printing for tail-folding, reductions, reverse/vector intrinsics, and fixed-order recurrences, but they do not modify LoopVectorize or VPlan implementation code.
Changed symbols: llvm/test/Transforms/LoopVectorize/VPlan/RISCV/vplan-vp-intrinsics-fixed-order-recurrence.ll; llvm/test/Transforms/LoopVectorize/VPlan/RISCV/vplan-riscv-vector-reverse.ll; llvm/test/Transforms/LoopVectorize/VPlan/PowerPC/vplan-force-tail-with-evl.ll; llvm/test/Transforms/LoopVectorize/VPlan/AArch64/sve-tail-folding-forced.ll; llvm/test/Transforms/LoopVectorize/VPlan/AArch64/sve2-histcnt-vplan.ll; llvm/test/Transforms/LoopVectorize/VPlan/AArch64/widen-call-with-intrinsic-or-libfunc.ll; llvm/test/Transforms/LoopVectorize/VPlan/AArch64/vplan-printing.ll; llvm/test/Transforms/LoopVectorize/predicated-early-exits-interleave.ll
Behavioral change: No runtime behavior change is visible in the retrieved hunks; the patch adds/updates tests that lock in VPlan printing and recipe ordering expectations.; The tests explicitly check for phi-like recipes such as EXPLICIT-VECTOR-LENGTH-BASED-IV-PHI, FIRST-ORDER-RECURRENCE-PHI, ACTIVE-LANE-MASK-PHI, and WIDEN-REDUCTION-PHI appearing in specific positions relative to non-phi recipes.; This can detect ordering regressions in VPlan construction, but the commit itself does not show code that would fix or introduce the assertion.
Assertion or trace link: Found phi-like recipe after non-phi recipe; LoopVectorize/VPlan assertion; VPlan recipe ordering; phi-like recipes; non-phi recipe
Reproducer link: Crash-62b480.cpp at -O3 is described as crashing in LoopVectorize/VPlan; The retrieved hunks only add tests for RISCV/PowerPC/AArch64 VPlan printing and do not mention the reproducer source
Pass or subsystem link: LoopVectorize; VPlan; VPlan printing tests; tail folding / predication / reductions
Causal explanation: The issue is about an assertion in VPlan recipe ordering during vectorizer plan construction. This commit only adds tests that exercise and check VPlan ordering across several scenarios, so it is related to the same subsystem and symptom space, but there is no implementation change in the retrieved hunks to directly cause or fix the crash.
Causal confidence: 0.78
Build risk: test-only change; new VPlan printing coverage under high-risk LoopVectorize paths; multiple target-specific checks for RISCV, PowerPC, and AArch64; no implementation hunks in retrieved diff

+; RUN: opt -passes=loop-vectorize -debug-only=loop-vectorize \
+; RUN: -prefer-predicate-over-epilogue=predicate-else-scalar-epilogue \
+; RUN: -mtriple=riscv64 -mattr=+v -riscv-v-vector-bits-max=128 -disable-output < %s 2>&1 | FileCheck --check-prefix=IF-EVL %s

+define void @first_order_recurrence(ptr noalias %A, ptr noalias %B, i64 %TC) {
+; IF-EVL: VPlan 'Initial VPlan for VF={1},UF>=1'

+; IF-EVL-NEXT: Live-in vp<[[VTC:%[0-9]+]]> = vector-trip-count
+; IF-EVL-NEXT: Live-in ir<%TC> = original trip-count
+; IF-EVL-EMPTY:
+; IF-EVL: ir-bb<entry>:
+; IF-EVL-NEXT: Successor(s): scalar.ph, vector.ph
+; IF-EVL-EMPTY:
+; IF-EVL: vector.ph:
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:  EMIT-SCALAR vp<[[VF32:%[0-9]+]]> = trunc vp<[[VF]]> to i32
+; IF-EVL-NEXT: Successor(s): vector loop
+; IF-EVL-EMPTY:
+; IF-EVL: <x1> vector loop: {
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:   vector.body:
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:     EMIT vp<[[IV:%[0-9]+]]> = CANONICAL-INDUCTION
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:     EXPLICIT-VECTOR-LENGTH-BASED-IV-PHI vp<[[EVL_PHI:%[0-9]+]]> = phi ir<0>, vp<[[IV_NEXT:%.+]]>
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:     FIRST-ORDER-RECURRENCE-PHI ir<[[FOR_PHI:%.+]]> = phi ir<33>, ir<[[LD:%.+]]>
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:     EMIT-SCALAR vp<[[AVL:%.+]]> = phi [ ir<%TC>, vector.ph ], [ vp<[[AVL_NEXT:%.+]]>, vector.body ]
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:     EMIT-SCALAR vp<[[PREV_EVL:%.+]]> = phi [ vp<[[VF32]]>, vector.ph ], [ vp<[[EVL:%.+]]>, vector.body ]
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:     EMIT-SCALAR vp<[[EVL]]> = EXPLICIT-VECTOR-LENGTH vp<[[AVL]]>
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:     vp<[[ST:%[0-9]+]]> = SCALAR-STEPS vp<[[EVL_PHI]]>, ir<1>
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:     CLONE ir<[[GEP1:%.+]]> = getelementptr inbounds nuw ir<%A>, vp<[[ST]]
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:     vp<[[PTR1:%[0-9]+]]> = vector-pointer inbounds nuw ir<[[GEP1]]>
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:     WIDEN ir<[[LD]]> = vp.load vp<[[PTR1]]>, vp<[[EVL]]>
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:     WIDEN-INTRINSIC vp<[[SPLICE:%[0-9]+]]> = call llvm.experimental.vp.splice(ir<[[FOR_PHI]]>, ir<[[LD]]>, ir<-1>, ir<true>, vp<[[PREV_EVL]]>, vp<[[EVL]]>)
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:     WIDEN ir<[[ADD:%.+]]> = add nsw vp<[[SPLICE]]>, ir<[[LD]]>
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:     CLONE ir<[[GEP2:%.+]]> = getelementptr inbounds nuw ir<%B>, vp<[[ST]]>
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:     vp<[[PTR2:%[0-9]+]]> = vector-pointer inbounds nuw ir<[[GEP2]]>
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:     WIDEN vp.store vp<[[PTR2]]>, ir<[[ADD]]>, vp<[[EVL]]>
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:     EMIT-SCALAR vp<[[CAST:%[0-9]+]]> = zext vp<[[EVL]]> to i64
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:     EMIT vp<[[IV_NEXT]]> = add vp<[[CAST]]>, vp<[[EVL_PHI]]>
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:     EMIT vp<[[AVL_NEXT]]> = sub nuw vp<[[AVL]]>, vp<[[CAST]]>
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:     EMIT vp<[[IV_NEXT_EXIT:%.+]]> = add vp<[[IV]]>, vp<[[VFUF]]>
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:     EMIT branch-on-count  vp<[[IV_NEXT_EXIT]]>, vp<[[VTC]]>
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:   No successors
+; IF-EVL-NEXT: }
+; IF-EVL-NEXT: Successor(s): middle.block
+; IF-EVL-EMPTY:
+; IF-EVL: middle.block:
+; IF-EVL-NEXT: Successor(s): ir-bb<for.end>
+
+; IF-EVL: Cost of 0 for VF vscale x 4: FIRST-ORDER-RECURRENCE-PHI ir<[[FOR_PHI]]> = phi ir<33>, ir<[[LD]]>
+; IF-EVL: Cost of 4 for VF vscale x 4: WIDEN-INTRINSIC vp<[[SPLICE]]> = call llvm.experimental.vp.splice(ir<[[FOR_PHI]]>, ir<[[LD]]>, ir<-1>, ir<true>, vp<[[PREV_EVL]]>, vp<[[EVL]]>)
+entry:
+  br label %for.body
+
+for.body:
+  %indvars = phi i64 [ 0, %entry ], [ %indvars.next, %for.body ]
+  %for1 = phi i32 [ 33, %entry ], [ %0, %for.body ]
+  %arrayidx = getelementptr inbounds nuw i32, ptr %A, i64 %indvars
+  %0 = load i32, p

+; CHECK-NEXT:      REPLICATE store ir<%add>, ir<%arrayidx4>
+; CHECK-NEXT:    Successor(s): pred.store.continue

top_candidates.subject: [VPlan] Fix masked_cond expansion.
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This change fixes masked_cond expansion in VPlan by swapping the operands of a LogicalAnd used during concrete recipe conversion. The patch also updates LoopVectorize tests to reflect the new operand ordering in several predicated early-exit and single-exit cases.
Changed symbols: VPlanTransforms::convertToConcreteRecipes; VPInstruction::LogicalAnd; predicated-single-exit.ll checks; predicated-multiple-exits.ll checks; predicated-early-exits-interleave.ll checks
Behavioral change: Changes the generated LogicalAnd operand order from (operand, mask) to (mask, operand) during masked_cond expansion.; Adjusts expected select ordering in LoopVectorize tests for predicated exits/interleaving, indicating a semantic change in how predicates are combined or emitted.
Assertion or trace link: LoopVectorize; VPlan; masked_cond expansion; predicated early exits; select ordering
Reproducer link: Affects predicated single-exit and multiple-exit vectorization patterns.; Test diffs show changed select operand ordering in early-exit/interleave scenarios.
Pass or subsystem link: LoopVectorize; VPlanTransforms
Causal explanation: This is plausibly related to VPlan construction and predicate handling, which can influence recipe ordering and downstream assertions. Still, the retrieved hunks only show a LogicalAnd operand swap and test expectation updates; they do not directly mention phi-like recipes or the specific ordering assertion. The connection to the reported crash is therefore moderate and indirect.
Causal confidence: 0.42
Build risk: High-risk LoopVectorize/VPlan transformation; Changes predicate composition semantics; Multiple regression tests updated for predicated exits; Could affect codegen for masked/early-exit loops

steps.subject: [VPlan] Fix wrap-flags on WidenInduction unroll (#187710)

evidence: Touches induction unrolling and VPlan recipe generation, but mechanism is wrap-flag correctness
Same subsystem, yet no direct phi-like recipe ordering connection
features: VPlanUnroll, meta:core-llvm, path:flang/test/Integration/unroll-loops.f90, path:flang/test/Lower/HLFIR, path:llvm/lib/Transforms/Vectorize, path:llvm/test/Transforms/LoopVectorize
selection.diff_summary:
Summary: This patch fixes wrap-flag propagation for widened inductions in VPlan unrolling. It adds explicit no-wrap flag queries to VPlan IR flags, then uses those flags when creating explicit vector-length arithmetic and when unrolling widen-induction recipes, preserving unsigned/signed wrap semantics for integer inductions and fast-math flags for FP cases.
Changed symbols: VPIRFlags::hasNoWrapFlags; VPIRFlags::getNoWrapFlags; UnrollState::unrollWidenInductionByUF; VPlanTransforms::addExplicitVectorLength
Behavioral change: Preserves no-wrap metadata when cloning or expanding widened induction arithmetic.; Separates fast-math flag handling from integer wrap-flag handling in unroll logic.; Changes the arithmetic flags attached to generated add instructions in VPlan transformations.
Assertion or trace link: LoopVectorize/VPlan assertion; recipe ordering assertion; phi-like recipe after non-phi recipe
Reproducer link: crash at -O3; LoopVectorize/VPlan plan construction; induction-related vectorization
Pass or subsystem link: LoopVectorize; VPlan; VPlanUnroll
Causal explanation: This commit is in the same VPlan unroll/vectorizer subsystem, but its visible effect is on wrap flags rather than recipe ordering. It could affect plan construction indirectly because induction recipes are central to VPlan layout, yet the retrieved hunks do not show any direct manipulation of phi-like recipe ordering. The connection to the assertion is therefore weak.
Causal confidence: 0.31
Build risk: Touches core induction-unroll semantics; Changes IR flags on generated arithmetic, which can alter optimization and verification behavior; Multiple LoopVectorize tests updated for expected nsw/nuw output

top_candidates.subject: [VPlan] Fix wrap-flags on WidenInduction unroll (#187710)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This patch fixes wrap-flag propagation for widened inductions in VPlan unrolling. It adds explicit no-wrap flag queries to VPlan IR flags, then uses those flags when creating explicit vector-length arithmetic and when unrolling widen-induction recipes, preserving unsigned/signed wrap semantics for integer inductions and fast-math flags for FP cases.
Changed symbols: VPIRFlags::hasNoWrapFlags; VPIRFlags::getNoWrapFlags; UnrollState::unrollWidenInductionByUF; VPlanTransforms::addExplicitVectorLength
Behavioral change: Preserves no-wrap metadata when cloning or expanding widened induction arithmetic.; Separates fast-math flag handling from integer wrap-flag handling in unroll logic.; Changes the arithmetic flags attached to generated add instructions in VPlan transformations.
Assertion or trace link: LoopVectorize/VPlan assertion; recipe ordering assertion; phi-like recipe after non-phi recipe
Reproducer link: crash at -O3; LoopVectorize/VPlan plan construction; induction-related vectorization
Pass or subsystem link: LoopVectorize; VPlan; VPlanUnroll
Causal explanation: This commit is in the same VPlan unroll/vectorizer subsystem, but its visible effect is on wrap flags rather than recipe ordering. It could affect plan construction indirectly because induction recipes are central to VPlan layout, yet the retrieved hunks do not show any direct manipulation of phi-like recipe ordering. The connection to the assertion is therefore weak.
Causal confidence: 0.31
Build risk: Touches core induction-unroll semantics; Changes IR flags on generated arithmetic, which can alter optimization and verification behavior; Multiple LoopVectorize tests updated for expected nsw/nuw output

top_candidates.subject: Revert "[VPlan] Extract reverse mask from reverse accesses" (#189637)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This revert removes reverse-mask handling from LoopVectorize/VPlan memory widening and restores prior behavior for reverse widened loads/stores and EVL/mask optimization. The hunks show the commit backing out creation of a reversed mask in tryToWidenMemory, threading the Reverse flag into widened load/store recipes, and adjusting VPlanTransforms to avoid EVL conversion for reverse memory recipes.
Changed symbols: VPRecipeBuilder::tryToWidenMemory; VPWidenLoadRecipe; VPWidenStoreRecipe; optimizeMaskToEVL; VPRecipeWithIRFlags::getCostForRecipeWithOpcode; getCostForIntrinsics
Behavioral change: Stops synthesizing VPInstruction::Reverse for masks during memory widening.; Removes reverse-specific handling from widened load/store recipe construction.; Adds guards so EVL/mask optimization does not apply to reverse widened loads/stores.; Removes a cost-model special case that treated reverse mask intrinsics as zero-cost.
Assertion or trace link: LoopVectorize; VPlan; phi-like recipe; non-phi recipe; recipe ordering; assertion
Reproducer link: crash at -O3; VPlan assertion during vectorizer plan construction

Summary: This change refactors VPlan handling for AnyOf/Or-style reductions so that the Or reduction is represented and propagated as a ComputeReductionResult recipe, and the epilogue-vector-loop planner treats ComputeReductionResult differently when it is only an internal input to ComputeAnyOfResult. It also updates VPlan recipe generation to read the reduced value from lane 0 for the new reduction form, and adjusts reduction-chain skipping logic so intermediate ComputeReductionResult recipes are not mistaken for final results.
Changed symbols: UnrollState::unrollBlock; VPlanTransforms::optimizeFindIVReductions; LoopVectorizationPlanner::addReductionResultComputation; preparePlanForEpilogueVectorLoop; VPInstruction::generate; VPInstruction::getNumOperandsForOpcode
Behavioral change: Introduces a dedicated ComputeReductionResult recipe for Or reductions used by AnyOf handling instead of folding them directly into ComputeAnyOfResult.; Changes epilogue-plan selection to include ComputeReductionResult only when it is not merely feeding a ComputeAnyOfResult.; Changes reduction generation to fetch the reduced operand via State.get(..., VPLane(0)) rather than manually OR-reducing multiple operands in VPInstruction::generate.; Updates reduction-chain filtering so intermediate ComputeReductionResult nodes are skipped unless they are the final result.
Assertion or trace link: LoopVectorize; VPlan; ComputeAnyOfResult; ComputeReductionResult; phi-like recipe ordering; non-phi recipe
Reproducer link: crash at -O3; early-exit / AnyOf reduction vectorization paths; vectorizer plan construction and epilogue planning
Pass or subsystem link: LoopVectorize; VPlan; VPlanTransforms; VPlanRecipes; VPlanUnroll
Causal explanation: The patch is clearly in the same LoopVectorize/VPlan area implicated by the crash, and it changes how reduction recipes are constructed and ordered in plans. However, the retrieved hunks do not mention phi-like recipe ordering directly, nor do they show an assertion fix for 'Found phi-like recipe after non-phi recipe'. The connection is therefore indirect: this commit could affect recipe ordering and plan shape around reductions, but the evidence only supports a related VPlan reduction-path change, not the exact assertion.
Causal confidence: 0.42
Build risk: Touches core LoopVectorize/VPlan recipe construction and plan transformation logic; Changes operand interpretation for call/reduction recipes; Adds new control-flow-sensitive handling in epilogue vector loop preparation; Includes new/updated LoopVectorize VPlan tests for early-exit reductions

top_candidates.subject: [VPlan] Optimize FindLast of (binop %IV, live-in) by sinking. (#183911)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This change refactors VPlan's find-last induction-variable sinking optimization so it can recognize and sink expressions derived from widened IVs, clone the sunk scalar expression when needed, and build the reduction/select chain using the vector-region exiting value directly. It also updates epilogue tests to match the new VPlan output.
Changed symbols: VPlanTransforms::optimizeFindIVReductions; getExpressionIV; cloneBinOpForScalarIV; VPBuilder; VPReplicateRecipe; VPScalarIVStepsRecipe
Behavioral change: The optimization now detects when FindLastExpression is an expression of a widened IV and uses the underlying IV for SCEV reasoning.; When sinking such an expression, it creates a new select in the loop block that tracks the underlying IV directly and updates the backedge value.; The middle-block reduction result is built from the select result, and the vector-region exiting value may be cloned from the scalar IV expression.
Assertion or trace link: VPlan; recipe ordering; phi-like recipe; non-phi recipe
Reproducer link: LoopVectorize/VPlan plan construction; epilogue vectorization test coverage; find-last IV sinking
Pass or subsystem link: VPlanTransforms; LoopVectorize; VPlan

That makes it relevant to a VPlan ordering assertion in general. However, the visible hunks are specifically about find-last IV sinking and select/reduction construction, not about phi-like recipes or the exact assertion text. top_candidates.subject: Reapply "[VPlan] Handle calls in VPInstruction:opcodeMayReadOrWriteFromMemory." (#191886)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit changes VPlan construction and VPInstruction handling for call instructions and memory-reading recipes. It adds helpers to identify the called function operand, teaches VPInstruction that calls may read/write memory based on the callee, tightens load-dereferenceability checks to treat VPIRBasicBlock as a memory-reading region, and introduces a separate mem-op widening decision pass that can convert load/store VPInstructions into widened or replicate recipes. It also moves invariant reduction-store handling out of the main VPlan build loop into a dedicated helper.
Changed symbols: VPlanConstruction.cpp::areAllLoadsDereferenceable; VPlanRecipes.cpp::getCalledFnOperandIndex; VPlanRecipes.cpp::getCalledFunction; VPInstruction::getNumOperandsForOpcode; VPInstruction::opcodeMayReadOrWriteFromMemory; VPRecipeBuilder::widenIfHistogram; VPRecipeBuilder::replaceWithFinalIfReductionStore; LoopVectorizationPlanner::tryToBuildVPlanWithVPRecipes
Behavioral change: Call VPInstructions now compute operand count by locating the callee operand, supporting both masked and unmasked call layouts.; Calls are classified as memory-reading/writing if the callee is not marked doesNotAccessMemory.; Load-dereferenceability analysis now treats VPIRBasicBlock as a boundary/exception alongside the middle block.; Memory widening is split into a separate transformation pass after initial VPlan construction.; Load/store recipes are no longer widened in the same place as other non-phi recipes; they are handled earlier or asserted as already handled.; Invariant reduction stores are extracted into a separate final-store recipe insertion path.
Assertion or trace link: LoopVectorize; VPlan; VPRecipe; phi-like recipe; non-phi recipe; recipe ordering; assert
Reproducer link: The issue is a LoopVectorize/VPlan assertion during plan construction at -O3.; This commit directly changes VPlan construction and recipe classification/order-sensitive handling, including moving memory-op transformations out of the main build loop.
Pass or subsystem link: LoopVectorize; VPlanConstruction; VPlanRecipes; VPlanTransforms
Causal explanation: This is strongly connected to the reported crash surface because it changes how VPlan recipes are classified, widened, and inserted, which can affect ordering invariants between phi-like and non-phi recipes. The added call-memory classification and the split mem-op widening pass are especially relevant to recipe sequencing. top_candidates.subject: [NFCI][VPlan] Split initial mem-widening into a separate transformation (#182592)

Summary: This commit refactors LoopVectorize's VPlan building by splitting initial memory widening into a separate transformation and by changing how non-phi recipes are widened. It adds a dedicated VPlanTransforms::makeMemOpWideningDecisions pass, inserts a new cost context, sets the insertion point for memory widening, broadens the set of recipes skipped as already transformed, and replaces inline store histogram/reduction-store handling with helper routines that can erase or replace recipes earlier in the pipeline.
Changed symbols: LoopVectorizationPlanner::tryToBuildVPlanWithVPRecipes; VPRecipeBuilder::tryToWidenMemory; VPRecipeBuilder::tryToCreateWidenNonPhiRecipe; VPRecipeBuilder::widenIfHistogram; VPRecipeBuilder::replaceWithFinalIfReductionStore; VPlanTransforms::makeMemOpWideningDecisions; VPlanTransforms.h; VPWidenCanonicalIVRecipe
Behavioral change: Initial memory-op widening is no longer performed inline with general recipe creation; it is deferred to a dedicated VPlan transformation.; The builder now explicitly sets the insertion point before widening memory operations.; Load/store recipes are asserted to have been handled before non-phi widening, reducing duplicate handling paths.; Recipes already transformed, including widened loads/stores and pointer recipes, are skipped in later passes.; Histogram stores and invariant reduction stores are handled through dedicated helper logic that may erase the original VPInstruction and optionally insert a final replicate recipe.

Summary: This commit makes several VPlan and LoopVectorize changes around canonical induction variables and lane-mask phi placement. It changes canonical IV handling from a typed VPCanonicalIVPHIRecipe pointer to a generic VPValue, preserves canonical IVs in register-usage analysis even when unused, updates canonical IV users when creating loop regions, adjusts explicit vector-length construction to use the canonical IV increment, and changes lane-mask phi insertion to occur at the start of the header block rather than after the canonical IV phi. It also simplifies some IV increment replacement logic in epilogue vector loop preparation.

Behavioral change: Changes canonical IV treatment so it is retained/updated as a region value and can be used even without direct users.; Moves lane-mask phi insertion to the beginning of the header basic block, which changes recipe/block ordering relative to other header phis.; Updates loop-region construction to replace outermost scalar phi uses with the region canonical IV and erase the old phi.; Adjusts IV increment handling and register-usage accounting to account for canonical IVs explicitly.
